nodes.source_text: Ni foam (thickness: 1 mm) was cut into 10 mm × 20 mm and 50 mm × 50 mm square sheets. The discs were ultrasonically cleaned in acetone, 0.1 M HNO3 and H2O for 15 min, respectively, followed by drying with a high-pressure nitrogen flow.

nodes.name: PBA deposition on Ni foam
nodes.procedure: PVP (0.35 g, 1 μmol), NiCl2·6H2O (35 mg, 0.15 mmol), and sodium citrate dihydrate (60 mg, 0.2 mmol) were dissolved in H2O (30 mL). Thereafter, the above-mixed liquid was dropwise added into 20 mL potassium ferricyanide solution (50 μmol, containing 16 mg of potassium ferricyanide). The cleaned Ni foam was placed into the mixed liquid and aged for 48 h to obtain Prussian blue analogues loaded Ni foam anode. The exposed surface of each Ni foam in contact with 8 mL of the mixed liquid is constantly set to 4 cm².

Thereafter, the above-mixed liquid was dropwise into 20 mL potassium ferricyanide solution (50 μmol, containing 16 mg of potassium ferricyanide). The cleaned Ni foam was placed into the mixed liquid and aged for 48 h to obtain Prussian blue analogues loaded Ni foam anode.

nodes.description: LSV comparison of biomass electro-oxidation vs OER in 1.0 M KOH

activation.value: twenty CV cycles 1-2 V vs RHE at 100 mV/s

nodes.source_text: Before the electrochemical study, the NiFe/Ni anode was activated through twenty circles of cyclic voltammetry ranging from 1 to 2V vs. RHE at 100mVs^{-1}... As shown in Fig. S6, the overpotentials at 10mAcm^{-2} for the electro-oxidation reaction of biomass is at least 160mV, smaller than that of OER... Especially, the ΔE of NiFe/Ni in an electrolyte containing FF is up to 200 mV

nodes.description: Two-electrode overall water splitting with photo-assisted HER cathode
nodes.source_text: linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves of NiFe/Ni coupled with Ni-TCPP/TiO2 in 1.0M KOH display an overpotential around 1.75V at 100mAcm^{-2} for overall water splitting. However, after adding 15mM of FF, the cell voltage is further reduced to 1.27V... long-term electrolysis was conducted at a constant current density of 10mAcm^{-2} to pass the charge of 144C. The catalytic conversion and selectivity of 2-furfural to 2-furancarboxylic acid are 96% and 90% respectively... the Faraday efficiency of the furfural electro-oxidation is around 60%
the overpotential of the Ni-TCPP/TiO2 electrode is 156mV at 10mAcm^{-2} without irradiation; however, it is decreased to only 26mV under Xe lamp (300W) irradiation

nodes.description: Electrochemical kinetics analysis (EIS, ECSA, Tafel) for furfural electro-oxidation
nodes.source_text: the furfural electro-oxidation curve exhibits a reduction in R_ct (24.1Ω cm^{-2}) up to four orders of magnitude from that of the pure OER curve (1.4×10^5 Ω cm^{-2}). ...the electrochemical surface area (ECSA) of the electro-oxidation of furfural (6.3mFcm^{-2}) is higher than that of pure OER (2.7mFcm^{-2})... the Tafel slope of NiFe/Ni in furfural electro-oxidation processes is lower (75mVdec^{-1}) than that of Ni foam (125 mVdec^{-1})

electrode_preparation.value: NiFe PBA dripped on glass carbon

nodes.source_text: The electrolyte (1.0M KOH with 15mM furfural) was saturated with N2 while circulating through the cell at 10mL min^{-1}. The data were collected by potentiostatic method, and the electrolysis time under an applied potential were all set to 120s.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanocubes assembled on Ni foam surface with side length of about 150 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in SEM images, nanocubes are assembled upon the Ni foam surface (Fig. 1b and S4), and their side length is about 150 nm (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD pattern of the catalyst matches the simulated PXRD pattern of Ni₂[Fe(CN)₆] (JCPDS: 14-0291).
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 1c, the PXRD pattern of the catalyst meets the simulated PXRD pattern of Ni₂[Fe(CN)₆] (JCPDS: 14-0291).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Fe 2p peaks at 708.3, 721.2 and 723.6 eV correspond to Fe(II)-(C≡N)x and Fe(III) respectively; Ni 2p deconvoluted into Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectra of Fe 2p can be deconvoluted into three peaks at 708.3, 721.2 and 723.6 eV, which correspond to Fe (II)-(C≡N)x, and Fe(III) respectively (Fig. 1d) [24]. Meanwhile, the high-resolution Ni XPS spectrum is deconvoluted into Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 peaks (Fig. 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR signals display a signal at g-value of 2.004, indicating lattice deformations introduce polarons in Ni₂[Fe(CN)₆].
nodes.evidence_snippet: ESR signals of NiFe/Ni anode display a signal at g-value of 2.004, indicating that the lattice deformations of Ni₂[Fe(CN)₆] introduce polarons (Fig. S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS O 1s shows Ni(III)-O peak at 528.9 eV confirming Ni(II) oxidized to Ni(III); oxygen vacancies peak at 531.9 eV in reconstituted material.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak of Ni(III)-O at 528.9 eV can be observed on the XPS of O 1s, which further reveals that Ni(II) in original NiFe/Ni electrode can be oxidized to Ni(III) after the electrochemical process (Fig. 3b). Noted that, the peaks of oxygen vacancies at 531.9 eV can be observed on the XPS O 1s spectra (Fig. 3d).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows Fe concentration of 63 μg mL⁻¹ in electrolyte and not detected in NiFe/Ni anode after reconstitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ICP-OES results show that the concentration of Fe element in the electrolyte is 63 μg mL⁻¹ and not detected in the NiFe/Ni anode after electrochemical reconstitution.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area increases from 4.42 m² g⁻¹ to 5.29 m² g⁻¹ after electrochemical reconstitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 3d, the surface areas are increased from original 4.42 m² g⁻¹ to 5.29 m² g⁻¹ after electrochemical reconstitution of NiFe/Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows NiFe/Ni nanocubes transform into hollow structure with tiny NiO particles coated on surface after reconstitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 3e, the NiFe/Ni nanocubes are transformed into a hollow structure after reconstitution, and some tiny particles (NiO) are coated on the surface of nanocubes.

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ Raman shows NiOOH bending and stretching vibrations of Ni³⁺-O at 475 and 555 cm⁻¹ when potential >1.4 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When the potential is higher than 1.4 V, NiOOH can be observed by the bending and stretching vibrations of Ni³⁺-O (475 and 555 cm⁻¹).

properties.pattern: blue-to-red gradient indicating temperature-dependent absorbance changes

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ PXRD shows NiFe/Ni (200) peak at 17.6° disappears; NiOOH (001) peak intensity increases after potential reaches 1.4 V (JCPDS #06-0141).
nodes.evidence_snippet: When NiFe/Ni was exposed to 1.0 M KOH, its characteristic (200) peak at 17.6° disappears. On the contrary, the intensity of the fingerprint (001) peak of NiOOH (JCPDS #06-0141) increases after the potential reaches 1.4 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: ESR spectrum verifies oxygen vacancies exist in reconstituted ν-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: ESR spectrum in Fig. S23, further verifies the oxygen vacancies exists in reconstituted NiOOH (ν-NiOOH) obtained via electrochemical reconstitution of NiFe/Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Furfural TPD shows desorption temperature of 135.5°C for ν-NiOOH, higher than Ni foam (114.6°C), with higher TCD signal intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 6b, the desorption temperature of ν-NiOOH for furfural was 135.5°C, significantly higher than that of Ni foam (114.6°C).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ ATR-FTIR shows furfural ring stretching at 1541 and 1508 cm⁻¹; 2-furfuralcarboxylic acid peaks at 1451 and 1508 cm⁻¹ appear >1.2 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 6c, the peaks at 1541 and 1508 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the furfural ring stretching vibration peaks. Moreover, the peaks at 1451 and 1508 cm⁻¹ are attributed to the asymmetric stretch vibration peak of 2-furfuralcarboxylic acid.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows Rct of 24.1 Ω cm⁻² for furfural electro-oxidation vs 1.4×10⁵ Ω cm⁻² for OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In contrast, the furfural electro-oxidation curve exhibits a reduction in Rct (24.1 Ω cm⁻²) up to four orders of magnitude from that of the pure OER curve (1.4×10⁵ Ω cm⁻²).
